content.text: The document expressly meets the preferred position. No redline needed.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position outright: there is no minimum purchase commitment or take-or-pay exposure on Customer. Clause 2.1 (p0013) states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies, that Customer pays only for Services ordered under a mutually executed Order Form, and that a decision not to place another Order Form is neither a breach nor a shortfall. Clause 7.1 (p0026) reinforces this by barring Vendor from imposing any platform, support, administration or minimum-use charge not identified in the Order Form, and clause 12.3 (p0051) records that Customer has given no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, or minimum-volume commitment. Sections 4 and 8 contain no committed spend, non-reducible seat count, or volume floor; Order Forms bind only when signed by both Parties (p0019) and renew only subject to Customer's thirty-day non-renewal right (p0035), so no multi-year lock-in arises. The only "shortfall" references (p0095, p0096) sit in the audit provisions and operate as a usage true-up for undisputed underpayment rather than a take-or-pay penalty, which is consistent with the playbook's preference for true-ups over penalties. The fee-related MFN in 7.6 and the reciprocal audit mechanics run in our favour or are neutral, so nothing here is flagged. Separately noted for awareness only, and not under this rule: clause 7.7 (p0032) imposes a fifteen-percent-per-week liquidated damages charge on Customer for late payment, which is a late-payment/interest issue properly addressed under the payment-terms rule rather than double-flagged as a volume commitment.
